title: introduce-thrift-wardrobe-defaults-and-quant-profiles
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Customers repeatedly ask for safer, opinionated defaults that balance latency SLOs and unit cost for common workload classes (chat, short-form generation, embedding-heavy search). This PR introduces a small, extensible defaults layer ("Thrift Wardrobe") that ships curated batching and cache presets, plus a companion quantization profile registry and a dry-run CLI that simulates unit-economic impact for tenant-level defaults. Goals: 1) provide low-friction, production-ready defaults teams can opt into; 2) expose quant profiles chosen for predictable regressions under strict quality budgets; 3) allow ops/SEs to preview cost/latency tradeoffs via a deterministic dry-run before applying defaults.

What this PR does (high level): Adds an Econ Defaults compiler that composes: - batch_shape presets tuned per model family and median seq lengths - cache window defaults (prefix vs. full-token caching) and KV retention policies - quant_profile registry (float16/4-bit/8-bit heuristics) with compatibility tags and safety cutoffs - a CLI `rw-econ dry-run` which replays a small sampled tenant trace and emits projected token-cost, p50/p95 latency, and estimated quality delta metrics (using historical eval harness signatures). Also wires telemetry: new econ.default.apply and econ.dryrun.report events and unit-tests + integration test harness for the CLI.

Checklist: - [x] defaults compiler implementation - [x] quant profile YAML registry and loader - [x] dry-run CLI and deterministic simulator - [x] unit tests for presets and registry loader - [x] integration smoke for telemetry events - [x] docs: quickstart and caveats

Backward compatibility and safety: Defaults are opt-in and gated behind feature flags per-tenant. Quant profiles include conservative fallback tags (e.g., "safe-rollback"), and the dry-run emits explicit quality-regression alarms when eval-signature delta > configured threshold. No runtime path will change unless the tenant sets the default or an operator enables the flag.

Related work and context: builds on prior economizer/autotune efforts (ENG-7621, PRs: introduce-cost-autoguider, prefills heuristics). Addresses customer asks in SUP-204 (large enterprise wanting simple defaults for Dedicated clusters).

Usage notes: Example CLI: `rw-econ dry-run --tenant-id=acct_123 --preset=chat-short --quant=4bit-aggressive --sample-size=1000 --out=report.json`. The report includes per-model projection and recommended safe-fallback explicitly.

Migration: None required. Operators can import presets-as-code via the existing defaults API; the compiler exposes a deterministic JSON that can be audited and checked into tenant configs.
